Let \(a\) be the number of students younger than Petya. Then Petya has \(2a\) older students, so
\[
n=a+2a+1=3a+1,
\]
so \(n\equiv 1 \pmod 3\).

For Katya, let \(c\) be the number of students older than her. Then the number younger than her is \(3c\), so
\[
n=3c+c+1=4c+1,
\]
so \(n\equiv 1 \pmod 4\).

Thus \(n\equiv 1 \pmod{12}\). Since \(20<n<30\), the only possibility is
\[
n=25.
\]

\boxed{25}
